title: Case: Customer holds a drop-off receipt for a return the carrier has never scanned
context: A cordless vacuum from Tallowmere Goods was approved for return. The refund is released automatically on the first carrier scan of the return label, and the return window is close to ending.
initial_request: this is a joke. receipt says 14/04 15:22, 1 parcel, ref ending 945, stamped by the shop. i did what i was told. your tracking says 'label created - not yet received' so either the shop lost it or your driver did, not my problem. window shuts monday and then what, im out £189 AND the hoover?? refund it today or tell me its lost so i can claim.

events.body: Return approved for TG-945 (cordless vacuum). Return label DL-945 issued 10 Apr. Refund is released by the Refunds team on first carrier scan of the label. Return window closes 27 Apr.
dropped it at the pickup point at farrow st newsagent on the 14th. got a paper receipt. still no refund??
Please give the refund status for TG-945. The customer reports dropping return DL-945 at the Farrow Street pickup point on 14 Apr.

No carrier scan against DL-945 so nothing has triggered. We don't refund on a customer's say-so or a shop receipt. If the label gets a scan it releases automatically. Unscanned labels are a carrier matter, that's Parcel trace team, Plover Arc Logistics.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Parcel trace team, Plover Arc Logistics
acceptable_actions.summary: Request a trace of return label DL-945 from the Farrow Street pickup point, giving the receipt details against the absence of any carrier scan, and flag the 27 April return window.

must: Gives the customer's receipt details (Farrow Street pickup point, 14 Apr 15:22, one parcel, reference ending 945, shop stamp) and that DL-945 has no carrier scan since label creation
Asks the Parcel trace team to trace the parcel, including the handover from the pickup point, and report a finding
Mentions that the return window closes on 27 Apr
must_not: Tells the customer the refund will be paid, or gives a date for it
Tells the customer the return is lost
Asks or instructs the Refunds team to release the refund on the strength of the receipt
States that the pickup point or the driver lost the parcel, or that the customer did not hand it in
Tells the customer the return window will be extended
expected.reference_message: Please trace return label DL-945 (Tallowmere order TG-945, cordless vacuum). The customer, Nkem Adeyo, reports handing it in at the Farrow Street newsagent pickup point and holds a paper receipt: 14/04, 15:22, one parcel, reference ending 945, stamped by the shop. Tracking shows label created, not yet received, and there has been no carrier scan of any kind. The receipt and the scan record conflict and I am not treating the parcel as lost or as not handed in. Please check the pickup point's handover for 14 Apr onward and any unscanned returns from that location, and tell me the finding. The merchant's return window closes on 27 Apr and the refund depends on a first carrier scan, so timing matters.

rationale: A stamped drop-off receipt says the parcel entered the network and the carrier's record says it never did; neither proves where the vacuum is. The Refunds team will not act without a scan and points to the Parcel trace team for unscanned labels. Promising the refund, declaring the return lost, or pressing Refunds to pay on the receipt would each settle the conflict by assertion.
